scope: Bounded passing-side selection at the first observed WR live-ball avoidance encounter.

observedFailure.description: A moving defender repeatedly forced the receiver left of its planned right-side catch route. After throw receipt, catch forecasts alternated between reachable and sprint-pending pursuit while collision avoidance retained a left bypass. No catch or airborne action was completed.
observedFailure.importantDistinction: The first catch avoidance state had no prior passing side. Clearing stale side state would not change that decision.

reproducedDefect.description: The original entry rule used body position to choose a side, then ranked the best endpoint direction on that side. Its score did not include the time needed to turn and move along that checked path. A slightly higher eventual-direction score selected a slower bounded approach.

entryGate: Controller explicitly opts in only for WR, Live phase and an observed ball arc.
The catch target and future arrival deadline are finite and the requested direction agrees with that target.
No existing passing side is locked; already selected bypasses retain their normal stability behavior.
The character is outside the near-contact band and both existing side candidates are available.
comparison: Replay at most 15 ordinary helper steps per side within 250 ms, using only current numeric body positions and velocities.
Use the actual caller heading and movement request for the first projected step.
Use the dispatch snapshot speed to interpret already-scaled movement, then cap the next speed after sprint release. No new sprint acknowledgement or extra speed is credited.
Keep existing turn limits, collision checks, physical movement scales and field bounds.
Unknown velocity, an early clear-path transition, a passed target or another invalid projection retains the original side.
Select the alternative only when both forecasts remain valid and it improves projected target progress by at least 0.1 stud.
implementation.nativeInputChanges: No jump, dive, capsule, character-speed, floor-state or catch-claim override.
implementation.observability: Numeric side scores, projected progress/clearance and step budget are attached to the existing throttled playerAvoidance event. No additional event stream or UI is added.

failures: recorded new catch encounter compares actual bounded turns instead of a slightly larger instantaneous score
mirrored catch has the same checked progress and mirrored side
a selected passing side remains locked on later observations
projected walking output is interpreted once at dispatch speed
unknown retained trajectory is not treated as worse than a known alternative
inactive old heading does not replace the caller heading on the first projected step
bounded side comparison is explicitly limited to WR live-ball approaches
bounded comparison diagnostics use the existing avoidance event

validation.labelsUse: Native outcomes are evaluation labels only; they are never inputs to selection.

additionalMovingBlockControl.observedSequence: No safe movement, resumed a checked bypass 33 ms later, then returned to the catch path.
additionalMovingBlockControl.lastStateLimitation: The last state lacks the prior clear-frame debounce timestamp. Before and after are identical for the reconstructed state, but it does not exactly reproduce the observed final return. The entry-only branch is excluded by the retained side for any debounce timestamp.

limits: The measured correction is a bounded movement-progress improvement, not proof that every missed catch is fixed.
The 250 ms comparison extrapolates current opponent velocity; opponents can react or change direction immediately.
The new projected minimum clearance is about 0.011 stud above the existing threshold. This does not create a guarantee against native body interaction or replication uncertainty.
The preserved successful controls cover the initial avoidance decision, not randomized full-match counterfactual outcomes.
Offline Lua timing is measured in the local replay runtime; native Roblox scheduling and float precision can differ.
Known contested catch awards, native airborne-state changes and missed-takeoff causes remain separate incident classes.

conditionalCatchReplay.interpretation: Conditional model feasibility only. The replay retains the recorded opponent trajectory and cannot reproduce how the opponent would react, native collision impulses/floor flags or authoritative catch arbitration.
